title: System
description: A system is a set of entry ids plus declared joints. It is the unit at which INTEGRATION is measured. Entries are the parts; a system is an assembly of them. The integration report over a system reports coverage and gaps and emits no combined score and no ranking of the entries in it, because ranking parts is the supremacy frame SYSTEMS_ANALOGY.md was written against.

status.description: illustrative: assembled to exercise the report, not a claim that these parts ever ran together. proposed: someone is arguing this is an assembly. attested: the assembly is evidenced.

membership_rule.description: The stated rule by which membership was decided, so that the set is reproducible by someone else and is not a preference. Required: a system whose membership rule is unstated cannot be checked.

layer_role.description: The role this entry plays IN THIS SYSTEM. A role is relational, so the same entry can carry different roles in different assemblies. If the entry also declares layer_role, the two are compared and a disagreement is reported rather than resolved.

role_basis.description: Required whenever layer_role is declared here. Where the role assignment came from. A role with no basis is a guess with a field around it.

runs_on.description: Entry ids or layer_role tokens this member requires beneath it, in this system. Empty array declares that nothing sits beneath it. Absent declares nothing.

runs_on_basis.description: Required whenever runs_on is declared here.

joints.description: Declared connections between two members. A joint is entry-to-entry. Layer-level dependency is carried by runs_on and is not a joint. An empty list is a finding, not a formality: it says the assembly has members and no declared connections between them.
